jobs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Create ONLY the three-ken long-pike ashigaru (三間槍足軽) transparent troop art. Square 1000 x 1000 pixel canvas.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the user's ORIGINAL small Japanese Sengoku strategy-game troop illustration and is the PRIMARY STYLE, foreground identity, costume and pose reference. Image 2 is only a guide for the broad arrangement of one large front soldier with two quieter rear soldiers; do NOT copy its cartoon faces, repeated poses, short finished spearheads, or overly clean thick comic outlines.
STYLE: return to Image 1's understated Japanese historical strategy-game illustration: mature faces, modest black ink contours, restrained flat/cel shading, muted green clothing, simple dark lacquer armor with small ochre/gold details, slight hand-painted texture, readable small-scale silhouette. Not photographic, not rendered 3D, not realistic military oil painting. Also not cute, rounded, exaggerated comic/cartoon art. Keep head/hand proportions natural. Preserve the foreground soldier's original black jingasa with plain gold oval, green patterned sleeves, white headcloth, dark simple armor, and original upward-diagonal pike-bearing pose.

MOST IMPORTANT NEW WEAPON REQUIREMENT:
The user has explicitly RESTORED the ORIGINAL STEEP UPWARD-RIGHT ANGLE, around 55–65 degrees from horizontal, because it displays the longest shaft along the canvas diagonal. Do NOT use a low, level, downward or horizontal thrusting angle.
These are extremely long three-ken pikes. Extend each wooden pole FAR BEYOND the image edges. The main spear is a perfectly straight long continuous wooden shaft from lower-left through both grasping hands toward upper-right; it continues out through the TOP border as plain wooden shaft. Its metal spearhead is OUTSIDE the frame and MUST NOT be drawn inside the square. The other two pikes likewise continue beyond the top or upper-right border with their tips offscreen, rather than becoming short complete spears. We deliberately see only a portion of each roughly three-adult-heights-long weapon. Never shorten a pole to fit, never put a decorative metal cap where a shaft reaches the border. Shafts must be slender and rigid, with one uninterrupted straight axis on both sides of hands. No curved pole, kink, melting, interrupted alignment, or giant metal blade.

COMPOSITION AND VARIATION:
One dominant foreground ashigaru anchored to the LOWER LEFT, cropped naturally at left/bottom if useful, with two smaller, quieter soldiers in the MIDDLE RIGHT and RIGHT REAR. Use the transparent upper half for the long diagonal poles. The rear pair must be distinctly different PEOPLE and POSES, not scaled clones.
- Foreground: match the original figure's alert expression and raised forward hand, solid contrasting dark armor, strongest detail.
- Middle rear: younger clean-shaven man, slightly turned head, headcloth visible, different elbow bend and two-hand spacing, a modest narrower stance.
- Far rear: older lean man with different jaw/face and slight stubble, a differently angled jingasa and less headcloth, different green-gray sleeve pattern/armor lacing, a more upright staggered stance and a lower hand position on his OWN pike.
Keep all three recognizably the SAME ashigaru unit with simple matching equipment; do not turn the rear soldiers into elite samurai or different troop types. Their clothing shades and armor details can differ subtly. Rear colors are desaturated/lower-contrast so the front remains dominant; bodies are solid, not translucent ghost copies. All three long pikes tilt in a consistent upward-right formation but need not be exact parallel clones. Maintain separation so each pole traces unambiguously to its owner.
The art later fits a 1000-square area on a board-game tile. A commander counter can cover x=200..1000, y=0..800, so retain meaningful parts of the foreground clothing/armor along the left and bottom 200px strips. Do not draw the covering counter.

ANATOMY: plausible shoulder-elbow-wrist chains, fingers naturally wrapping the rigid shafts, coherent weight-bearing knees/ankles. Each man has his own two arms and two legs without fusions. Waist sidearms remain sheathed, with a continuous rigid outline and at most a very subtle natural single blade curve; no hooked/wavy scabbards. Keep equipment simple enough to inspect.
OUTPUT: genuine transparent alpha background, no white rectangle or checkerboard, no scenery/ground/paper/clouds, no UI/frame/labels/numbers/text/flags/watermark. Avoid red/yellow edge contamination. This is ONE art asset containing the three-man formation, NOT a contact sheet.
